 Lakers urged to trade Bronny James instead of moving on from Knecht 
 2026-10-18 16:51 
 The Los Angeles Lakers must cut their roster down to 15 standard contracts ahead of the regular season. While Dalton Knecht has been considered a potential cut candidate, CBS Sports reporter Sam Quinn suggests trading Bronny James instead due to his offensive struggles.
 Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect - Scanpix 
 Credit IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect - Scanpix 
 Credit IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect - Scanpix 
 Add us on 
 Add us on 
 The Los Angeles Lakers are yet to make the decision on their 16 standard contracts ahead of their season opener against the Golden State Warriors on Wednesday.
 Schedule 
 Thu 
 02:00 
 Sat 
 02:00 
 With the Lakers needing to have 15 standard contracts to start the season, most have floated the name of Dalton Knecht as the player the Los Angeles team is trying to move on from.
 However, NBA reporter Sam Quinn of CBS Sports suggests that the Lakers should instead trade Bronny James rather than waiving Knecht.
 "If I were the Lakers, I'd be trying to trade Bronny right now to some owner who wants to sell some jerseys," Quinn wrote.
 "I'd rather keep Knecht on the books as possible trade salary than cut him and deal with dead money. The Lakers don't really need the James brand like other teams do."
 Quinn assessed Bronny's development so far
 JJ Redick Bronny James Lakers Credit AP - Scanpix Quinn expanded on Bronny James' development at this point, criticizing his offense and giving a defensive comparison that James is yet to reach.
 "Just hasn't reached the point of offensive viability through two years, and the defensive threshold is just so freaking high at that size that if he's never gonna make shots, he basically has to be a Jamal Shead-level pest to even justify a roster spot and he isn't," the reporter explained.
 Bronny has played in 5 preseason games for the Lakers, scoring 2.2 points and adding 2.4 rebounds, 2.8 assists in 16.4 minutes per game, while shooting 4-of-16 from the field.
